title: Full DAG visualization for Tier 3 parallel phase execution
summary: Architecture analysis for extending the pipeline DAG visualizer to render Tier 3 parallel plan phase execution as a true branching graph. The current visualizer renders a flat linear sequence (Refine -> Plan -> Implement -> PR) with Tier 3 sub-phases grouped by plan_phase_id inside the Implement box. This produces non-deterministic ordering for parallel phases and no branching structure. The recommended approach expands the Implement phase into its constituent sub-phases as first-class boxes in the DAG, connected with fan-out/fan-in connectors, while keeping the data model unchanged.

problem_statement.description: The current DAG visualizer in dag_visualizer.py renders a fixed 4-phase linear DAG (Refine -> Plan -> Implement -> PR). For Tier 3 (high-complexity) pipelines, the Implement phase runs multiple plan sub-phases, some in parallel, but this structure is invisible in the visualization. The current workaround groups agents by plan_phase_id inside the Implement box (lines 283-298 of dag_visualizer.py), producing a flat listing like 'phase-1: coder, tester... phase-2: coder, tester...' with two problems: (1) parallel sub-phases are shown in lock-acquisition order rather than sorted deterministically, and (2) there is no branching structure showing fan-out/fan-in for parallel phases.
goals: Render Tier 3 sub-phases as individual boxes in the DAG, each showing its own agent sequence and status
Display parallel sub-phases side-by-side with fan-out connectors from Plan and fan-in connectors to the post-phase section (reviewer_contract + integrator)
Display sequential sub-phases in single-column layout
Sort parallel sub-phases deterministically by phase ID, not lock acquisition order
Show per-sub-phase status symbols, agent waves, and timing
Show the reviewer_contract + integrator section as a separate box between sub-phases and PR
Maintain backward compatibility for Tier 1/2 pipelines (no sub-phases) and the compact/progress views
Update the SSE streaming and CLI tools (egg-pipeline-watch, egg-status) to render the new layout

dag_visualizer.mechanism: render_pipeline_dag() iterates PHASE_ORDER = [REFINE, PLAN, IMPLEMENT, PR], calling _render_phase_box() for each. Boxes are connected by vertical arrows. For Tier 3, _render_phase_box lines 283-300 partition agents by plan_phase_id into sub_phase_buckets and render them as labeled groups inside the Implement box.
dag_visualizer.key_issue: The Implement box is treated as a single monolithic phase. There is no concept of expanding it into multiple boxes with branching connectors. The sub_phase_buckets dict uses insertion order which is non-deterministic for parallel phases.

dependency_graph.mechanism: PhaseDependencyGraph.compute_waves() returns list[PhaseWave], each containing phase_ids that can run concurrently. PhaseWave.is_parallel() returns True if multiple phases share a wave. Phases within a wave are sorted by bisect.insort in topological_sort() (line 482), giving deterministic alphabetical ordering.
dependency_graph.key_insight: The wave computation already exists and produces exactly the grouping needed for visualization. The visualizer just needs to consume it.

pipeline_state.mechanism: Pipeline.phases is a dict[str, PhaseExecution]. PhaseExecution.agents is a list[AgentExecution]. Each AgentExecution has a plan_phase_id field for Tier 3 sub-phase tagging. Pipeline.complexity_tier indicates LOW/MID/HIGH.
pipeline_state.key_insight: All the data needed to render sub-phase boxes already exists in the pipeline state. Agents tagged with plan_phase_id can be grouped by sub-phase, and the PhaseDependencyGraph provides the branching structure.

contract_model.mechanism: Phase model has id (e.g., 'phase-1'), name, status, tasks, and dependencies (list of phase IDs). The contract's phases list defines the complete dependency graph.
contract_model.key_insight: Phase names and dependency info from the contract are needed for display labels and DAG structure.

tier3_dispatch.mechanism: _run_tier3_implement() loads the contract, builds PhaseDependencyGraph, computes waves, then executes phases either sequentially or in parallel waves using ThreadPoolExecutor. Each phase runs a full coder -> tester -> documenter -> checker -> reviewer cycle. After all phases, reviewer_contract and integrator run as top-level agents (no plan_phase_id).
tier3_dispatch.key_insight: The dispatch already uses the same wave structure we need for visualization. The contract is available in .egg-state/contracts/ and can be loaded by the visualizer.

sse_streaming.mechanism: SSEClientManager subscribes to EventBus, fans out to connected clients. Refresh cycle (1s) re-renders the full DAG and sends it if changed. The rendered DAG is a text string.
sse_streaming.key_insight: No structural changes needed to SSE. The refresh cycle already re-renders the full DAG text. A wider DAG will just be a wider string.

egg_pipeline_watch.mechanism: Connects to per-pipeline SSE endpoint. Receives rendered DAG text. Uses ANSI cursor control for in-place terminal updates.
egg_pipeline_watch.key_insight: The tool renders whatever DAG text it receives. No changes needed to the streaming logic, only to dag_visualizer.py output.

egg_status.mechanism: Multi-pipeline dashboard. Uses compact mode by default. Full DAG mode is optional via --verbose.
egg_status.key_insight: Compact mode is unchanged. Full DAG mode uses the same render_pipeline_dag() output.

classes: TestRenderPipelineDag — full DAG rendering with various states
TestWaveGrouping — wave-based agent grouping (implement, plan, refine)
test_coverage.gap: No tests exist for Tier 3 sub-phase branching visualization since it doesn't exist yet. The test for plan_phase_id grouping inside the Implement box is only indirect (via the sub_phase_buckets logic).

implementation_approaches.name: Expand Implement phase into sub-phase boxes in render_pipeline_dag (recommended)
implementation_approaches.description: Modify render_pipeline_dag() to detect Tier 3 pipelines (complexity_tier == HIGH and agents have plan_phase_id). When detected, instead of rendering a single Implement box, render: (1) the Plan box with a fan-out connector, (2) sub-phase boxes arranged by wave (parallel phases side-by-side, sequential phases stacked), (3) fan-in connector to a 'Review + Integrate' box for top-level agents (reviewer_contract, integrator), (4) the PR box. Use PhaseDependencyGraph to determine wave structure. Each sub-phase box uses the existing _render_phase_box rendering with its subset of agents. Add new helper functions: _render_tier3_section() for the multi-column layout, _render_fan_out() and _render_fan_in() for branching connectors, _render_side_by_side_boxes() for parallel phase boxes.
pros: Changes are concentrated in dag_visualizer.py — the primary file for visualization
Reuses existing _render_phase_box for sub-phase rendering — consistent look and feel
Leverages PhaseDependencyGraph.compute_waves() which already provides the exact grouping needed
SSE, CLI tools, and API endpoints require no changes — they already consume text output from render_pipeline_dag()
Tier 1/2 pipelines are completely unaffected — the expansion only triggers for Tier 3
Deterministic ordering comes naturally from PhaseDependencyGraph.topological_sort() which uses bisect.insort
The phase name and status can be derived from the contract and agent statuses
cons: Side-by-side ASCII box rendering requires careful width management and padding
Loading the contract from dag_visualizer creates a new dependency (currently it only reads Pipeline model)
Terminal width constraints may limit how many parallel phases can be shown side-by-side

implementation_approaches.name: Embed phase wave structure in Pipeline model, render from model alone
implementation_approaches.description: Add a new field to Pipeline model (e.g., phase_waves: list[PhaseWaveInfo]) populated by the orchestrator during Tier 3 dispatch. The visualizer reads this field directly without needing to load the contract. PhaseWaveInfo contains wave_number, phase_ids, phase_names, and is_parallel. The visualizer uses this data to render the branching DAG.
pros: No contract loading in the visualizer — all data is in the Pipeline model
Cleaner separation of concerns — orchestrator computes structure, visualizer renders it
PhaseWaveInfo can include derived data (phase names, overall phase status) for easier rendering
cons: Requires a model migration — adding a new field to Pipeline model
Duplicates information already available in the contract
Existing pipelines in flight would not have the new field — needs backward-compatible handling
The orchestrator would need to persist wave info during dispatch, adding logic to _run_tier3_implement

implementation_approaches.name: Separate Tier 3 DAG renderer
implementation_approaches.description: Create a new function render_tier3_dag() that produces a completely separate visualization for Tier 3 pipelines. render_pipeline_dag() detects Tier 3 and delegates to this function. The Tier 3 renderer builds the entire DAG from scratch using contract data, with no dependency on the linear phase rendering.
pros: Complete freedom to design the Tier 3 layout without constraints from the linear renderer
No risk of breaking existing visualization — linear renderer is untouched
cons: Significant code duplication — header, phase box rendering, status symbols, timing all need to be reimplemented or extracted
Maintenance burden — two parallel rendering paths that must stay in sync
Over-engineering — the linear renderer already does most of what's needed

recommended_approach.name: Expand Implement phase into sub-phase boxes in render_pipeline_dag
justification: Minimal blast radius — changes are concentrated in dag_visualizer.py with no model changes and no orchestrator changes
All downstream consumers (SSE, CLI tools, API) require zero changes since they already consume text output
Reuses existing infrastructure: _render_phase_box for sub-phase boxes, PhaseDependencyGraph for wave structure, _compute_wave_order for agent grouping within sub-phases
The contract loading dependency is manageable — the contract file is available in .egg-state/contracts/ which the orchestrator already manages, and the visualizer runs in the same filesystem context
Deterministic ordering is solved by using PhaseDependencyGraph.topological_sort() instead of dict insertion order
Backward compatibility is trivial — the expansion only triggers when Tier 3 agents with plan_phase_id are detected

_render_sub_phase_box.signature: _render_sub_phase_box(phase_id: str, phase_name: str, status: PipelineStatus, agents: list[AgentExecution], duration: str, total_duration: str, review_cycles: int, is_current: bool, use_ascii: bool) -> list[str]
_render_sub_phase_box.behavior: Renders a single sub-phase box similar to _render_phase_box but with a shorter label format showing the phase ID and name. Box width is constrained to fit in multi-column layouts. Each box shows its agents grouped by wave, status symbol, and timing.

_render_side_by_side.signature: _render_side_by_side(box_groups: list[list[str]], gap: int, left_margin: int, use_ascii: bool) -> list[str]
_render_side_by_side.behavior: Takes multiple box line-lists and renders them side-by-side. Pads shorter boxes with empty lines. Inserts a gap (spaces) between columns. Handles boxes of different heights by padding to the tallest. Returns combined lines. The left_margin parameter provides consistent indentation.
_render_side_by_side.key_detail: Each box's lines are already generated by _render_sub_phase_box(). This function only handles horizontal composition.

_render_fan_out_connector.signature: _render_fan_out_connector(num_branches: int, box_widths: list[int], gap: int, left_margin: int, use_ascii: bool) -> list[str]
_render_fan_out_connector.behavior: Renders the branching connector from a single point to N parallel boxes. Uses Unicode box-drawing characters (or ASCII fallback). Structure: vertical line from parent, horizontal line spanning all branches, vertical lines dropping to each branch. Example for 2 branches: '|' -> '+-+-+' -> '| |'.

_render_fan_in_connector.signature: _render_fan_in_connector(num_branches: int, box_widths: list[int], gap: int, left_margin: int, use_ascii: bool) -> list[str]
_render_fan_in_connector.behavior: Inverse of fan-out: renders vertical lines from each branch merging into a single point. Uses same character set as fan-out.

_render_tier3_implement_section.signature: _render_tier3_implement_section(pipeline: Pipeline, phase_waves: list[PhaseWave], phase_info: dict[str, dict], is_current: bool, use_ascii: bool) -> list[str]
_render_tier3_implement_section.behavior: Main orchestrating function for the Tier 3 section. Iterates over phase_waves. For each wave: if is_parallel(), renders boxes side-by-side with fan-out/fan-in connectors; otherwise renders a single-column box. Then renders the top-level agents box (reviewer_contract, integrator). Returns all lines. The phase_info dict maps phase_id to {name, status, agents, duration, etc.}.

_get_phase_dependency_info.behavior: Loads the contract for the pipeline's issue_number, builds PhaseDependencyGraph, computes waves. Extracts per-phase info by partitioning the Implement phase's agents by plan_phase_id. Computes per-sub-phase status from agent statuses (all complete -> complete, any running -> running, any failed -> failed, else pending). Returns None if pipeline is not Tier 3 or contract cannot be loaded. Falls back gracefully.
_get_phase_dependency_info.contract_loading: Uses egg_contracts.load_contract(issue_number, repo_path). The repo_path can be derived from environment or passed as a parameter. If contract loading fails, returns None to trigger fallback to the existing flat rendering.

render_pipeline_dag.change: After rendering the Plan box and its arrow, check if the pipeline is Tier 3 with sub-phase data. If yes, call _render_tier3_implement_section() instead of _render_phase_box(IMPLEMENT). Then render the arrow and PR box. If Tier 3 detection fails or returns None, fall back to the existing single Implement box rendering.
render_pipeline_dag.detection: Tier 3 is detected by checking: (1) pipeline.complexity_tier == ComplexityTier.HIGH, and (2) the Implement phase has agents with plan_phase_id set. Both conditions must be true.
render_pipeline_dag.fallback: If PhaseDependencyGraph cannot be built (contract not found, import error, etc.), fall back to existing rendering. This ensures the visualizer never crashes.

_render_phase_box.change: No changes needed. Sub-phase boxes use _render_sub_phase_box (a slimmed-down variant). The existing _render_phase_box continues to work for Refine, Plan, PR, and non-Tier-3 Implement.
_render_phase_box.alternative: Could add a 'compact' parameter to _render_phase_box to reuse it for sub-phases. But a separate function is cleaner since sub-phase boxes have different label format and width constraints.

render_compact_status.change: Minor enhancement: for Tier 3 pipelines, could show sub-phase progress in the compact line. Example: 'Refine -> Plan -> [Implement: 2/3] -> PR'. This is optional and can be deferred.
render_compact_status.note: The compact view is inherently a summary — detailed sub-phase info belongs in the full DAG view.

render_progress_bar.change: For Tier 3 pipelines, could weight the Implement phase by sub-phase completion. Example: if 2 of 3 sub-phases are complete, the Implement phase contributes 2/3 instead of 0.5. This is optional and can be deferred.
render_progress_bar.note: More accurate progress for Tier 3 but not required for the core visualization change.

generate_status_report.change: No changes needed. The DAG visualization in the report is just the text output from render_pipeline_dag(), which will now include the expanded Tier 3 layout.

sub_phase_status_derivation.description: Each sub-phase's status must be derived from its agents. The pipeline state does not store per-sub-phase status directly — only the overall Implement phase status and per-agent statuses.
sub_phase_status_derivation.algorithm: For agents with matching plan_phase_id: (1) if any agent has status FAILED -> sub-phase FAILED, (2) if any agent has status RUNNING -> sub-phase RUNNING, (3) if all agents have status COMPLETE -> sub-phase COMPLETE, (4) otherwise -> sub-phase PENDING. This mirrors how the orchestrator determines overall phase status.
sub_phase_status_derivation.phase_name: Derived from the contract's Phase.name field. If contract is unavailable, fall back to the phase_id (e.g., 'phase-1').

layout_algorithm.description: The side-by-side rendering algorithm must handle variable-height boxes and arbitrary numbers of parallel phases.
layout_algorithm.approach: For each parallel wave: (1) render each sub-phase box independently, (2) compute maximum height across all boxes, (3) pad shorter boxes with empty lines, (4) horizontally compose with gap spacing, (5) add fan-out connector above and fan-in connector below.
layout_algorithm.width_management: Each sub-phase box has a fixed minimum width (e.g., 25 chars) and a maximum width based on terminal width / number of columns. If too many parallel phases to fit, fall back to sequential rendering with a note.
layout_algorithm.terminal_width: Use shutil.get_terminal_size() for width detection. Default to 80 columns. For SSE streaming (not a terminal), default to 120 columns.

If the contract cannot be loaded (e.g., missing, corrupted, wrong format), the visualizer must fall back gracefully to the existing flat Implement box rendering
The visualizer must never crash — all new code paths must have error handling with fallback
Sub-phase boxes must be sorted by phase ID (phase-1, phase-2, ...) for deterministic ordering, matching PhaseDependencyGraph.topological_sort()
ASCII mode must be supported for all new rendering (connectors, boxes, etc.)
The render_pipeline_dag() function signature must not change — it takes (pipeline, use_ascii, include_header) and returns a string
generate_status_report() return structure must not change — the 'dag' field just contains the new text
No changes to Pipeline model, PhaseExecution model, or AgentExecution model — the visualization derives structure from existing data plus the contract
The visualizer runs in the orchestrator process — it has filesystem access to .egg-state/contracts/

Top-level agents (reviewer_contract, integrator) that have no plan_phase_id must be rendered in a separate box below all sub-phases, not inside any sub-phase box

risk_assessment.risk: Side-by-side ASCII rendering is complex and error-prone
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implement the _render_side_by_side helper as a pure function with comprehensive unit tests. Use simple padding logic (pad to max height, join with spaces). Handle edge cases: single column (no side-by-side needed), empty boxes, very wide boxes (truncate or wrap).

risk_assessment.risk: Contract loading adds a filesystem dependency to the visualizer
risk_assessment.mitigation: Wrap contract loading in try/except with fallback to flat rendering. The contract file is always present during pipeline execution (written by plan phase). Cache the loaded contract in-memory per pipeline_id to avoid repeated file reads on refresh.

risk_assessment.risk: Wide DAGs overflow terminal width for many parallel phases
risk_assessment.mitigation: For 4+ parallel phases, fall back to sequential (stacked) rendering with a '(parallel)' label. Or use a 2-row grid layout. Most Tier 3 pipelines have 2-3 parallel phases per wave.

risk_assessment.risk: SSE refresh performance degradation with more complex rendering
risk_assessment.mitigation: The existing refresh cycle already compares rendered strings to skip redundant sends. The additional rendering cost is O(num_phases) which is bounded (typically < 10 phases).

risk_assessment.risk: Connector character alignment breaks with different box widths
risk_assessment.mitigation: Normalize all sub-phase boxes in a parallel wave to the same width (max width in the wave). This simplifies connector math and produces clean visual alignment.

phase_outline.name: Core rendering helpers and single-column Tier 3 visualization
phase_outline.description: Implement _render_sub_phase_box, _get_phase_dependency_info, and _render_tier3_implement_section for sequential (non-parallel) sub-phases. Modify render_pipeline_dag to detect Tier 3 and delegate. Fix deterministic ordering by using PhaseDependencyGraph. Add tests for sequential sub-phase rendering, status derivation, deterministic ordering, and fallback behavior.

phase_outline.name: Side-by-side parallel rendering with fan-out/fan-in connectors
phase_outline.description: Implement _render_side_by_side, _render_fan_out_connector, _render_fan_in_connector. Update _render_tier3_implement_section to use these for parallel waves. Handle width constraints and fallback for many parallel phases. Add tests for parallel rendering, connector alignment, mixed sequential/parallel waves, ASCII mode, and terminal width handling. Optionally enhance compact view and progress bar for Tier 3.
